$comment: Market benchmarks (spec §2.2), as data. Each entry declares the packages it belongs to and a condition, so a formation comparison cannot surface inside a hiring package. Every percentage here was written for this prototype and is backed by nothing, so every entry is marked unsourced and sits below the release gate. A benchmark asserts a fact about the market — it is held to the same standard as clause text, and in production it needs an n= and a date as well as a source.

benchmarks.label: Founder vesting
benchmarks.detail: of companies at your funding stage ({{fundingName}}) use 4-year vesting with a 1-year cliff.

benchmarks.label: Founder vesting
benchmarks.detail: of companies at your funding stage ({{fundingName}}) use founder vesting. It matters most when a founder leaves early.

benchmarks.label: IP assignment at formation
benchmarks.detail: of companies in your industry assign founder IP at formation. Expected for an IP-critical business.

benchmarks.label: IP assignment at formation
benchmarks.detail: of companies in your industry assign founder IP at formation. Less common here, still worth doing.

benchmarks.label: Transfer restrictions
benchmarks.detail: of multi-owner entities restrict transfers with a right of first refusal.

benchmarks.label: Transfer restrictions
benchmarks.detail: of single-owner entities bother. Low value until you add an owner — but cheap to add now.

benchmarks.label: Deadlock provision
benchmarks.detail: of two-founder agreements include one, but deadlock appears in the majority of two-founder disputes.

benchmarks.label: Delaware formation
benchmarks.detail: of venture-track startups form in Delaware, largely for its case law and investor familiarity.

benchmarks.label: {{formStateLong}} formation
benchmarks.detail: of venture-track startups form in {{formStateLong}}. Delaware remains the default for institutional rounds.

benchmarks.label: Severability clause
benchmarks.detail: of commercial contracts include one.

benchmarks.label: Limitation of liability
benchmarks.detail: of master services agreements cap liability at fees paid in the preceding twelve months.

benchmarks.label: Enhanced cap for data breach
benchmarks.detail: of deals above $50k where personal data is in scope carry a separate, higher cap for confidentiality and security incidents.

benchmarks.label: Service levels
benchmarks.detail: of enterprise services agreements specify uptime or response targets with credits.

benchmarks.label: Transition assistance
benchmarks.detail: of enterprise agreements guarantee a priced exit period. Switching cost is what turns non-renewal into captive renewal.

benchmarks.label: Most favored pricing
benchmarks.detail: of enterprise agreements include it. Frequently asked for, usually traded away for a verifiable discount.

benchmarks.label: Data processing addendum
benchmarks.detail: of agreements where personal data is in scope attach one. For most buyers it is a precondition to signature.

benchmarks.label: Source code escrow
benchmarks.detail: of enterprise software agreements include it, and the share is falling as hosted delivery replaces on-premise.

benchmarks.label: Written offer with stated pay basis
benchmarks.basis: required by statute in several states
benchmarks.detail: is the practical floor. Several states require a written wage notice at hire, and California requires it for every non-exempt employee.

benchmarks.label: Board approval language in offers
benchmarks.detail: of offers mentioning equity state that the grant is subject to board approval. An offer letter cannot itself grant equity.

benchmarks.label: Severance in non-executive offers
benchmarks.detail: of non-executive employment agreements include severance. Where it exists it is almost always conditioned on a signed release.

benchmarks.label: Arbitration agreement
benchmarks.detail: of employment agreements include one. In California it must be a separate signed document and cannot reach harassment claims.

benchmarks.label: Harassment training on time
benchmarks.detail: of California employers at {{headcountBand}} complete the training inside the statutory window. The deadline is six months from hire or promotion.

benchmarks.label: Local ordinance compliance
benchmarks.detail: of California employers with staff in {{caCityName}} track the local ordinance layer separately from state law. It is the most commonly missed California obligation.
